_comment: UITraps MCP Server — client configuration examples. Transport: Streamable HTTP at /mcp.
_setup_instructions: 1. Get your API key from your UITraps subscription dashboard.
2. Copy the block for your AI client below into its config file.
3. Replace YOUR_API_KEY_HERE with your actual key.
4. Replace the URL host with your Railway deployment (e.g. https://YOUR-APP.railway.app/mcp), or use http://localhost:8000/mcp for local dev.

claude_desktop._setup: Claude Desktop reaches the server through the mcp-remote bridge helper (requires Node.js/npx). MERGE the mcpServers block below into your existing config — do not overwrite the file. Keep the trailing slash on /mcp/, and note there is NO space after the colon in the Authorization header (mcp-remote is sensitive to it on Windows). Fully quit Claude Desktop from the system tray and reopen after adding or changing the server.

claude_code._command: Run this in your terminal, then restart Claude Code:
claude_code._run: claude mcp add uitraps --transport http https://YOUR-APP.railway.app/mcp --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_HERE'

local_dev._note: For local development (backend running on port 8000):

available_tools.analyze_screenshots: Analyze 1–10 UI screenshots. 1 credit per image.
available_tools.analyze_figma: Analyze a Figma file by URL. 1 credit per frame.
available_tools.analyze_pdf: Analyze a PDF document. 1 credit per page.
available_tools.analyze_video: Analyze a screen recording. 1 credit per extracted frame.
available_tools.ask_about_traps: Ask questions about the UI Traps framework. Free.
available_tools.get_trap_detection_rules: Get the detection rules, severity, and fixes for the Traps from the knowledge base. Free.
